---
title: "Benchmark: a store in the cloud against a local copy"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = TRUE)
results <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path("..", "..", "bench", "results", paste0(name, ".parquet"))
  tibble::as_tibble(arrow::read_parquet(path))
}
cloud <- results("cloud")
counters <- results("cloud-counters")
knitr::read_chunk(file.path("..", "..", "bench", "cloud.R"))
has_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
med <- function(case, expression) cloud$median_s[cloud$case == case & cloud$expression == expression]
```

This article reads stored results; it does not run the benchmark. The script
is `bench/cloud.R`; its code is shown below as it was run.

## Question

A store kept in Google Cloud Storage is read by streaming: Arrow fetches the
byte ranges it needs from the bucket. How does that compare with
downloading whole files first, and with reading a local copy of the same
store? What does a first connection cost (new credentials and file system)
against a later one, and what does MD5 verification cost when the bucket
reports the MD5 of each object? The cost of `store_sync()` is not yet
measured (see Limits).

## Setup

```{r}
env <- cloud[1, grep("^env_", names(cloud))]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  item = sub("^env_", "", names(env)),
  value = vapply(env, function(v) as.character(v[[1]]), character(1)),
  row.names = NULL
))
```

One store of `r cloud$datasets[[1]]` catalog entries (98 small tables, a
table of 1e6 rows partitioned by year in `r cloud$sales_files[[1]]` files of
`r round(cloud$sales_bytes[[1]] / 1e6, 1)` MB together, 1e5 polygons and
their index table; `r cloud$store_objects[[1]]` files,
`r round(cloud$store_bytes[[1]] / 1e6, 1)` MB) is written to a local folder
and its files are copied unchanged under a random prefix of a test bucket,
removed at the end. Each measure is timed with `bench_run()` (five
repetitions, median reported).

- Connect: `store_connect()` to the local copy; to the bucket cold (the Arrow
  file system and the access token created again before every repetition,
  as in a new R session) and warm.
- Reads: `store_read()` streaming from the bucket; the dataset's files
  downloaded whole (`be_get()`) into an empty folder; `store_read()` of the
  local copy. Download-then-read is the sum of the last two.
- MD5: `be_md5()` of the table's files (object metadata on the bucket,
  hashing the files on the local copy), and `store_check()` without `x`
  (MD5, rows and schema from the Parquet footers).

## Results

```{r}
shown <- cloud[c("case", "expression", "run", "median_s", "min_s", "max_s")]
shown[4:6] <- lapply(shown[4:6], signif, 3)
knitr::kable(shown)
```

Streaming against download, in seconds:

```{r}
cases <- c("sales full", "sales year and columns", "polygons full")
compare <- data.frame(
  case = cases,
  stream = sapply(cases, med, "stream"),
  download = sapply(cases, med, "download"),
  local_read = sapply(cases, med, "local")
)
compare$download_then_read <- compare$download + compare$local_read
compare$stream_over_local <- compare$stream / compare$local_read
compare[-1] <- lapply(compare[-1], signif, 3)
knitr::kable(compare, row.names = FALSE)
```

For "sales year and columns" the download is of the one file of that year,
which the catalog names; streaming fetches only the three columns of it.

```{r, eval = has_ggplot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, fig.alt = "Grouped horizontal bars of median seconds for three reads: the full table, one year and three columns of the table, and the full polygons; bars for streaming from the bucket, download then local read, and local read only."}
library(ggplot2)
long <- data.frame(
  case = rep(compare$case, 3),
  method = rep(c("stream from bucket", "download, then read", "local copy"), each = nrow(compare)),
  seconds = c(compare$stream, compare$download_then_read, compare$local_read)
)
ggplot(long, aes(x = seconds, y = case, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Median seconds", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Work counters (backend calls and catalog files read):

```{r}
shown <- counters[counters$counter %in% c("backend_call", "catalog_read", "file_open", "bytes_down"), ]
shown <- stats::aggregate(n ~ case + expression + counter, data = shown, FUN = sum)
wide <- stats::reshape(shown, idvar = c("case", "expression"), timevar = "counter", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^n\\.", "", names(wide))
wide[is.na(wide)] <- 0
knitr::kable(wide, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Verdict

- Connect to the bucket: `r signif(med("connect", "connect_gcs_cold"), 2)` s
  cold, `r signif(med("connect", "connect_gcs_warm"), 2)` s warm, against
  `r signif(med("connect", "connect_local"), 2)` s for the local copy, with a
  catalog of `r cloud$datasets[[1]]` entries. A connection reads two catalog
  files and the store's settings, so its cost is a few round trips, not the
  size of the store.
- Full reads: streaming takes `r signif(med("sales full", "stream") / med("sales full", "local"), 2)`
  times as long as reading the local copy for the table, and
  `r signif(med("sales full", "stream") / (med("sales full", "download") + med("sales full", "local")), 2)`
  times as long as downloading the files first and reading them.
  The decoding of the rows in R costs the same on both sides, so streaming
  adds little to a full read.
- Filtered reads: one year and three columns streamed in
  `r signif(med("sales year and columns", "stream"), 2)` s, against
  `r signif(med("sales year and columns", "download") + med("sales year and columns", "local"), 2)` s
  to download that year's file and read it locally. Streaming is slower
  here because `store_read()` first opens an Arrow dataset over all
  `r cloud$sales_files[[1]]` files of the version (Arrow asks the bucket for
  each file's information and reads the first file's footer), and only then
  prunes the partitions and opens the remaining file again. On a 2-file copy
  of the table, opening the list took 0.36 s against 0.11 s when the schema
  was given; pruning on the catalog before the first open, and passing a
  schema, would remove most of this cost.
- MD5 verification on the bucket reads object metadata: `be_md5()` of
  `r cloud$sales_files[[1]]` files takes `r signif(med("md5 of sales files", "gcs"), 2)` s
  (`r signif(med("md5 of sales files", "local"), 2)` s to hash the local
  files); the whole integrity check takes
  `r signif(med("check sales", "gcs"), 2)` s on the bucket against
  `r signif(med("check sales", "local"), 2)` s locally, because it reads the
  Parquet footer of each file, one file after the other, over the network.
  MD5 verification itself is cheap on the bucket; the footers are the cost.

## Limits

- One machine and one network connection; its bandwidth to the bucket bounds
  every cloud number. Two other agents ran tests and rendered documents on
  the machine meanwhile.
- The cost of `store_sync()` is not yet measured. Its transfers are those
  of a write's upload and verification, measured in `benchmark-write.Rmd`.
- "Cold" means a new Arrow file system and a new access token in the same R
  session; the time to start R and load the package is not included.
- Spatial queries on the bucket are measured in `benchmark-spatial.Rmd`.
